A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIST/MDMS research, with matching authors, algorithms, principal theorems, and experiments. The full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments and ImageNet classification results in Section 5, plus parameter sweeps in Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v3 reports original synthetic-data experiments and ImageNet classification results in Section 5, with parameter sweeps retained in Appendix E.1.

M1.justification: The core GIST and GreedyIndependentSet procedures remain unchanged. However, Section 2.1 changes the auxiliary warm-up algorithm from a biased random choice between utility-only and diameter solutions to deterministically returning the better solution.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate weighted Gaussian points and single-shot ImageNet training-data selection, with the same appendix parameter-sweep coverage. Newly cited datasets such as LAION are contextual references, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained, with GIST-linear and GIST renamed GIST-margin and GIST-submod. The synthetic simple comparator references Section 2.1, whose selection rule changes from randomized to deterministic best-of-two. This revises its reported definition; the identical plots do not establish a rerun.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the reported ImageNet nearest-neighbor graph degree from 10 to 100. It also replaces the implicit very-large nonedge-distance convention with the maximum adjacent-pair distance. The initial 10% training subset, ResNet-56 model, and evaluated selection fractions remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The alpha and beta sensitivity sweeps in v2 Appendix D.1 and v3 Appendix E.1 are identical, including every plotted panel in Figures 2–3. No empirical ablation, robustness test, or error analysis is added. The new greedy counterexample is theoretical.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 reports three-trial averages without uncertainty values; v3 adds ± values throughout while retaining three trials. Their statistical meaning is not defined, and neither additional runs nor new significance tests are established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises several means: random at 30% changes from 66.27 to 66.23, and k-center at 50% from 73.09 to 73.01. Winners remain unchanged, and graph-based results accompany revised settings. v3 adds runtime figures and an unqualified GIST-submod-over-submod finding, although the retained 80% row shows 75.45 versus 75.91. Synthetic plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds Appendix B's counterexample for greedy that rejects negative gains, corrects the marginal-gain and intersection-graph definitions, and aligns weights and diversity coefficients in the linear hardness reductions. Principal approximation and hardness results remain. The general exact-1/2 remark is omitted, while Section 5.1 newly states an exact-2/3 guarantee for exhaustive synthetic thresholds.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the MDMS novelty claim, GIST approximation guarantees, complementary hardness results, Euclidean APX-completeness, and ImageNet application claim. Renaming min-distance diversification to max-min diversification and making its weighting explicit do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that the ImageNet submodular utility can be non-monotone and distinguishes its diversity component from div(S). It adds an interpretation of selection cost as negligible relative to training. Conversely, v2's warning that objective values across different k are not directly comparable is omitted.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents ImageNet epsilon=0.05, unit-length embeddings, explicit similarity conventions, and exhaustive pairwise thresholds for the synthetic experiment. Section 5.2 and Appendix E.2 add selection/training runtimes and threshold parallelism. These are additional disclosures; training hyperparameters are retained, while v2's linear-utility presorting optimization discussion is omitted.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially expands to non-monotone submodular maximization, distributed and low-adaptivity algorithms, historical dispersion results, asymmetric distances, and additional fairness formulations. The introduction also develops the relationship to Borodin et al. and adds Gollapudi and Sharma's utility-plus-max-sum predecessor, substantially enriching research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the introduction and related work, changes the title and diversification terminology, and reorganizes theoretical exposition. The full Theorem 4.1 proof moves to Appendix D.1 with a main-text sketch, and the experimental narrative is rewritten around consistently named GIST variants.

P2.justification: The document adopts NeurIPS formatting, substantially changing the author block, text width, typography, and content placement. Figure 1 is resized into a layout alongside text, and Table 1 is redesigned with uncertainty entries and renamed columns. The three figures retain their underlying plotted content.

improvement.justification: Expanded research context, corrected formal definitions and reduction parameters, and added implementation/runtime information make v3 clearer and easier to assess. These gains are tempered by undefined ± statistics, the lost cross-k comparison caveat, and the new overbroad GIST-submod comparison contradicted by Table 1 at 80%. With the principal results and empirical coverage retained, the net improvement is limited.
